Capital punishment in Slovakia ( Trest smrti ) was abolished in 1990 and the most severe punishment permissible by law is life imprisonment . Before that , capital punishment was common in Czechoslovakia , Slovak State , Austria-Hungary , Kingdom of Hungary and probably all previous political entities that existed in the area of today 's Slovakia . Eastern Silesia was formerly the Austrian crownland Austrian Silesia , which was occupied by Czechoslovakia after World War I . It had an area of 1,987 sq mi ( 5,146 km ² ) , with a population of 680,422 in 1900 . The capital was Opava . Plans for a plebiscite fell through , and the area was divided between Czechoslovakia and Poland . The territory was entered by the Czech military on 23 January 1919 , after negotiations with Poland broke down . A final agreement on the border was reached on 28 July 1920 .

[P5] Federal Assembly (Czechoslovakia)
The Federal Assembly was the federal parliament of Czechoslovakia from January 1 , 1969 to the dissolution of Czechoslovakia on December 31 , 1992 . It was Czechoslovakia 's highest legislative institution . Chapter 3 of the 1960 Constitution of Czechoslovakia recognized it as `` the supreme organ of state power and the sole statewide legislative body . ''
